key_insight: A conductive GaOx hole transport layer can be formed in situ during CuInSe2 co-evaporation, enabling efficient 1.0 eV bottom cells with low recombination and VOC above 550 mV.
engineering_relevance: This shows that high-performance chalcopyrite bottom cells can be optimized without Ag or heavy alkali additions, supporting simpler tandem-compatible device stacks.
method: Formed GaOx as a hole transport layer by ion exchange during absorber co-evaporation
Tested whether extra Cu, Na, or sputter oxygen flow were needed for GaOx conductivity
Analyzed the structural state of GaOx and its impact on solar-cell performance
evidence_signal: The optimized device achieved an active-area efficiency above 16% and a record-certified VOC of 552 mV for a 1.0 eV CuInSe2 bottom cell.
watch_item: The conductive behavior of GaOx appears to depend on its formation conditions and partly crystalline structure, so transferability to other back-contact stacks may be limited.
paper_title: What enables GaOx as hole transport layer for a 16 percent 1.0 eV CuInSe2 Bottom Cells with VOC above 550 mV?
